title: House of Five Leaves
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Edo-period Japan, the shy, unlucky ronin Akitsu Masanosuke (Masa) becomes bodyguard to Yaichi, leader of the Five Leaves, a gang whose main business is kidnapping. Masa is uneasy with the crimes but drawn to the outlaws, and Yaichi's violent past with another gang eventually catches up with them as the law closes in (Viz blurb via AniList/MU; ANN review of vol. 8).
life_message: Integrity and loyalty to friends can matter more than rank or the law, but past wrongs must still be faced.

content.note: Kidnapping gang; 'only one swordfight' in the finale and a threat of the executioner's blade (ANN); MU Murder/s. Series 'barely relies on violent fight scenes' (ANN).
Tragic pasts and pursuit by authorities (ANN; AniList Tragedy).
Red-light district and prostitution settings (MU; AniList Oiran rank 60); ANN does not mention sexual content. LGBTQ+ Themes tag (spoiler, rank 20) to verify.
Bars and drinking places (MU Bar/s) (to verify).
Masa's social anxiety (MU Social Phobia); tragic pasts.
Sympathetic gang kidnaps for profit (blurb, ANN); law catches up with Yaichi (ANN).

dominant: Integrity of a gentle ronin; found family among outlaws; reckoning with past crimes

frames.aligns: Masa's integrity and self-giving for friends; past sins must be faced.
frames.concerns: Kidnapping gang presented sympathetically; prostitution setting.

frames.aligns: Humility of Masa; repentance themes around Yaichi's past.

frames.concerns: Outlaws as heroes; prostitution and drinking settings.

frames.aligns: Grace-like hope on the final page (ANN).
Sin and its consequences portrayed truthfully.
Law catching up shows civil righteousness.
Question of using ill gains for altruism (ANN).
Subtle moral vision of integrity among sinners.
Karma of past deeds returns; quiet introspection.

frames.concerns: Kidnapping (a capital crime in Torah); prostitution.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Yaichi settles scores with his former boss (ANN), but Masa avoids fights.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Outlaws living outside lord and law (blurb, ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to the gang as family (AniList Found Family; ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Ronin serving lords; gang led by Yaichi (blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Edo-period samurai customs (MU Edo Period, Samurai).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Hungry ronin takes job to survive (blurb).

folkways.japan: Edo-period samurai service, a ronin's loss of status and quiet, implied emotion reflect Japanese historical norms and the series' understated style.

delivery.evidence: ANN: dialogue short, 'loaded with meaning', 'almost poetic', and can be hard to follow.
delivery.note: Ginta, a former victim, asks whether crime is forgivable if gains are used well, so the case against the gang is heard (ANN).

winners_losers: Masa's integrity and the gang's bonds earn sympathy, but Yaichi's past crimes are not excused and the law closes in (ANN).
to_verify: Depiction of the red-light district, prostitution and drinking (MU tags only).
ANN review covers volume 8; earlier volumes unchecked.
